finding: No test stores a valid park_until or started_at in an agent entry; a validator that rejects every ISO time passes
why: AC-012 requires each agent entry to carry a park-until time, yet only the invalid value tomorrow is exercised and only None is asserted, so the accept path of the iso kind is untested.
fix: Add a case that records park_until=2026-10-19T18:38:12Z and a started_at in the same form, reads them back equal, and refuses a near-miss such as 2026-10-19 18:38:12Z.
evidence: mutant: manifest.py _kind_ok iso branch return isinstance(value, str) and _ISO.fullmatch(value) is not None replaced by return False; 83 passed (SURVIVED). Tests have agent(park_until="tomorrow") (refused) and assert entry["park_until"] is None

finding: No test proves the publish is write-then-rename; a direct in-place write passes all 83 tests
why: The acceptance bullet on half-written manifests (ADR-0003: every write goes to a temporary file that is then renamed) has no test: test_no_temporary_file_is_left_after_a_write only lists the run directory, which an in-place write also leaves clean.
fix: Add a test that fails a publish midway (monkeypatch os.replace to raise, or json.dumps to raise after the temp exists) and asserts the old manifest bytes are intact and no temp file remains.
evidence: mutant in a scratch copy: scripts/team/manifest.py _publish temp = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.{os.getpid()}.{uuid.uuid4().hex}.tmp") replaced by temp = path; afk-python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_team_manifest.py: 83 passed (SURVIVED)

finding: A manifest file with invalid UTF-8 raises a bare UnicodeDecodeError, not ManifestError
why: `read_text` sits outside the `json.loads` try and its except clauses catch only FileNotFoundError and OSError, so callers that handle ManifestError (read_manifest, every write) crash on a corrupt file.
fix: Catch UnicodeDecodeError (or ValueError) around `read_text` and raise ManifestError naming the path.
evidence: `text = _patient(path.read_text, "utf-8")` / `except FileNotFoundError: return None` / `except OSError as exc: raise ManifestError(...)`. Failing input: manifest.json holding bytes b'\xff\xfe{'; read_manifest raises UnicodeDecodeError.

finding: Possible lost update: the lock-ownership check is not atomic with the publish, and a steal can evict a fresh lock
why: A writer that stalls past LOCK_STALE after the check at line 276 (or a third contender that mkdirs while `_steal_if_stale` holds the lock renamed away at lines 202-212) lets 2 writers hold the lock and the later publish overwrites the earlier one, and `_release` (lines 234-240) can unlink or rmdir a successor's owner file or folder.
fix: Make the stale-steal fence stronger (heartbeat the lock mtime during the write, or re-verify ownership immediately before and after os.replace and republish on loss) and make `_release` tolerate a replaced lock without touching it.
evidence: `if _owner(lock) not in (token, None):  # the lock was taken from this writer: redo under a fresh one` then `_publish(path, result)` on the next statements; `_steal_if_stale`: `os.rename(lock, grave)` ... `if _owner(grave) != judged:  # a fresh lock replaced the stale one: give it back` -> `os.rename(grave, lock)` falls through to `shutil.rmtree(grave)` when the give-back fails. Failing input: 3 writers, the holder stalls >10s (LOCK_STALE) between line 276 and the replace. (also reported by spec-fidelity: Lock-loss check and publish are not atomic, so a steal between them can still lose an update)

criterion: blast radius: changed public symbol with no named consumer
finding: adopt_manifest has no consumer named in any later contract and no wiring IOU
why: AC-015 adoption is a public entry point, but 0010 Consumes only record_entry and `.claude/wiring-ious.md` has no row, so no plan step is bound to call it.
fix: Add a `0003-manifest-module scripts/team/manifest.py#def adopt_manifest(` Consumes line to 0010-team-entry-script (or a wiring IOU anchored to it).
evidence: 0010-team-entry-script.md:124 `- 0003-manifest-module scripts/team/manifest.py#def record_entry(` is its only 0003 Consumes line; D-48 chose adopt_manifest as an extra public function; grep of plan/00{10,12,25}*.md for `adopt_manifest` finds nothing.

criterion: blast radius: changed public symbol with no named consumer
finding: remove_process has no named consumer; cleanup contract Consumes only move_entry
why: D-48 justified it by 'cleanup removes a process entry through this module', yet 0012 and 0010 name no Consumes line for it, so the kill-list removal path is unbound.

evidence: 0012-cleanup.md:61 `- 0003-manifest-module scripts/team/manifest.py#def move_entry(` is the only 0003 Consumes line; D-48 rationale: 'AC-015 needs an explicit takeover, and 0010's Acceptance says cleanup removes a process entry through this module'; grep for `remove_process` in plan/*.md outside 0003/DECISIONS/JOURNAL finds nothing.

finding: No boundary cases for the int and ostime kinds, or for a colon or NUL in names
why: Negative pids, boolean pids, a numeric started_at and a name with a colon are rules in _kind_ok and _name that no test exercises, and mutants dropping them survive.
fix: Add parametrized cases: pid=-1, pid=True, pid=1.5 refused; a process started_at given as a float accepted; names a:b and one holding NUL refused by manifest_path and checkpoint_path.
evidence: scratch mutants: int kind clause value >= 0 removed -> 83 passed; not isinstance(value, bool) removed -> 83 passed; ostime numeric branch replaced by False -> 83 passed. test_unsafe_names_are_refused parametrizes only the five names empty, dotdot, a/b, a-backslash-b and dot

finding: The adopt-first guard is tested only for a missing run directory, not for a directory with no manifest
why: record_entry, move_entry and remove_process reach _existing when the directory exists and the manifest does not, and removing that raise leaves all tests green.
fix: Create the run directory without a manifest and assert record_entry, move_entry and remove_process each raise ManifestError matching adopt_manifest.
evidence: mutant: manifest.py _existing raise ManifestError(f"no manifest for {feature}; call adopt_manifest first") replaced by returning an empty manifest; 83 passed (SURVIVED). Test calls record_entry(tmp_path, FEATURE, agent()) where tmp_path has no feature directory

finding: Stale-lock test never checks the redo after a lock is taken from a live writer and never checks the write landed
why: The _owner(lock) not in (token, None) redo guard in _write is the only defence when a live but slow writer loses its lock, and removing it leaves every test green; the test also asserts only that the lock is gone, not that the entry was recorded.
fix: Assert the agent entry is present after the steal; add a test where the lock owner file is swapped during change and the write is redone under a fresh lock, or where two contenders steal one stale lock and exactly one wins.
evidence: mutant: manifest.py _write guard if _owner(lock) not in (token, None): replaced by if False:; 83 passed (SURVIVED). Test ends with assert not lock.exists() and assert not list(... glob("manifest.lock.stale*"))

criterion: Fragile test / weak proof that the losing writer waits (SDD section 7)
finding: The live-lock test does not prove the writer waits, and no test shows a waiting writer proceeds after release
why: Acceptance says while the mutex is held the losing writer waits; a writer that gives up at once raises the same ManifestBusy, and only the stale-lock and race tests happen to kill that mutant.
fix: Assert elapsed time >= LOCK_WAIT in the give-up test, and add a test that releases the lock from a thread after about 0.2 s and asserts the blocked record_entry then succeeds.
evidence: mutant: manifest.py _acquire end = time.monotonic() + LOCK_WAIT replaced by end = time.monotonic(); test_a_live_lock_makes_the_writer_wait_then_give_up still passed (only test_a_stale_lock_is_stolen and test_two_racing_writers_lose_no_update failed)

criterion: Acceptance: public interface is record, move and read, and no caller learns of the lock
finding: ManifestBusy and the LOCK_WAIT/LOCK_STALE constants surface the lock to callers
why: SDD §8 row says 'no caller learns of the lock (S-49)', yet a caller must catch an exception named for the lock and gets a message naming the lock folder.
fix: Keep the failure signal but name it for the write (for example ManifestWriteTimeout) and keep the lock path out of its message, or record the exposure as a decision in plan/DECISIONS.md.
evidence: class ManifestBusy(ManifestError): """The manifest's lock stayed held by a live writer past `LOCK_WAIT` seconds."""; raise ManifestBusy(f"manifest lock {lock} held past {LOCK_WAIT:g}s")

criterion: blast radius: changed public symbol with no named consumer
finding: checkpoint_path has no named consumer in any later contract
why: AC-024 needs the path built by the module, but the plan names no subtask that calls it, so the checkpoint location may be rebuilt elsewhere.
fix: Name the consuming subtask in a Consumes line for `def checkpoint_path(`, or add an IOU anchored to AC-024.
evidence: grep for `checkpoint_path` and `checkpoints/` in plan/00{10,12,25}*.md finds no Consumes line; the only in-repo reference is scripts/tests/test_team_manifest.py:628.

finding: A real permission error on mkdir is reported as a lock held past 30s
why: Catching PermissionError for every platform turns a read-only or unwritable run directory into a 30-second wait that ends in a misleading ManifestBusy.
fix: Retry PermissionError only while the lock folder exists or for a short bounded count, then raise a ManifestError naming the permission failure.
evidence: `except (FileExistsError, PermissionError):  # Windows refuses a lock folder still being deleted` ... `raise ManifestBusy(f"manifest lock {lock} held past {LOCK_WAIT:g}s")`. Failing input: run directory with no write permission.

finding: A failed owner-file write leaves the lock folder held, and a failed publish leaves a temp file
why: After `os.mkdir(lock)` succeeds, an exception from the owner write (line 230) propagates before `_write`'s try/finally, so no release runs and other writers wait for LOCK_STALE; likewise an OSError inside `open`/`write`/`fsync` in `_publish` (lines 253-257) skips the `temp.unlink`, leaving a `manifest.json.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp` beside the manifest.
fix: Wrap the owner write in try/except that rmdirs the lock, and move the temp unlink into a try/finally covering the whole write.
evidence: `_patient((lock / "owner").write_text, token, "utf-8")` / `return token`; `with open(temp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:` precedes the only `temp.unlink(missing_ok=True)`, which sits in the os.replace handler. Failing input: disk full during the write.

criterion: Acceptance: a resume or a replacement is a new entry, never an edge back
finding: record_entry merges fields into an existing entry whatever its state, including the terminal cleaned
why: SDD §6 says a retry or resume is a new entry with a new agent-id, but a repeat agent-id silently rewrites the closed line's role, stage, pid and handle instead of being refused.
fix: Refuse an update to an entry in state cleaned (or a new-entry call that names an existing agent-id), or record in DECISIONS.md that updates to terminal lines are allowed.
evidence: found.update(entry)  # reached for any found['state'], incl. 'cleaned'; SDD §6: 'A resume or a replacement is a new entry in starting, never an edge back (S-213)'
